reasoning: docs/SPEC-001-graph.md sections 2 and 3. The engine reasons over relationships and there is nowhere to store them: today only decision.question_id exists and nothing populates it. One generic edge table rather than one per relationship, because DuckBrain declared tables need explicit columns and never introspect, so a narrow fixed shape keeps new edge kinds from forcing a mid-run migration. Columns: id(E-###### fixed-width), project_id, kind(opens|closes|satisfies|affects|breaks|derives_from|references|blocks), src_kind, src_id, dst_kind, dst_id, confidence(double, -1 when asserted by a person or rule rather than a model call), source(gate|impact|human|rule), note, created_at. Plus the facet table (F-######, project_id, question_id, facet(data|failure|ownership|cost|test|who_else), status, closed_by, note). Acceptance: `auger init` declares both tables idempotently and the live namespace exposes them at /api/ns/auger/tables; an edge round-trips through the declared-table API with its kind/confidence/source intact; inserting an edge whose src_id does not exist is REFUSED rather than silently stored.

reasoning: docs/SPEC-001-graph.md section 4 BEAT 4 and section 5. This is the mechanic that closes branches, and the engine is not one without it. When a question becomes answered|linked|moot: (a) every question with a derives_from edge from it is re-examined - if its blockers are resolved and it is now answerable from existing evidence it is GATED and linked rather than asked, otherwise it becomes newly askable; (b) when a decision is invalidated by a breaks edge, every question that decision closed becomes moot with the reason recorded, and that change propagates recursively. Engineering calls already concluded in the spec: branches DO reopen automatically when the answer that closed them is invalidated, with the reason recorded, because a stale closed branch silently reads as done and is worse than an open one. Acceptance: a question whose parent decision is invalidated by a breaks edge becomes moot with a reason naming the edge; the cascade reaches grandchildren; a question with an unresolved `blocks` edge is never surfaced by ask; a question that becomes answerable after a parent closes is LINKED by the gate rather than asked.
title: [P1] propagation: closure and moot cascades — SPEC-001 BEAT 4

reasoning: docs/SPEC-002-bundles.md section 1. The fleet's projects come in bundles (Bane subgoal) and the IMPACT pass currently searches ONE namespace, so a decision about a shared contract is invisible to the siblings that must honour it. Two tables plus one field: bundle(id B-01, name, description, contract, status), bundle_member(id BM-0001, bundle_id, project, role owner|consumer|test-target, note), and decision.scope (project|bundle; empty = project, which is the unchanged default). Membership is a table and not a column because a project can belong to several bundles (a harness is both an ecosystem member and its own project). Acceptance: `auger init` declares both tables idempotently; a bundle-scoped decision round-trips with its scope intact; the default for an existing decision row is project (no behaviour change on migration); a bundle_member naming a project with no scheduler row is REFUSED with a clear error.
title: [P1] bundle model: bundle + bundle_member tables, and decision.scope (project|bundle) — SPEC-002 1

reasoning: docs/SPEC-002-bundles.md sections 2.1 and 2.2. The two behaviours that make bundling worth having. (a) GATE searches EVERY member's namespace: evidence = recall_many([ns(m) for m in bundle_members(p)], q) - this is cross-project decision dedupe, so if terminal-jail already decided how a sandbox isolates the filesystem, bunker LINKS that answer instead of re-deciding it and drifting; the satisfies edge gains src_project so the reader sees it came from a sibling. (b) IMPACT crosses the boundary for bundle-scoped decisions only: a project-local decision never crosses (or every answer reaches every project and the pass is quadratic again), and a breaks edge INTO A SIBLING IS AN ESCALATION, NOT A SILENT CHANGE - the engine records the break and surfaces it, it never rewrites another project's spec. Depth triage for a bundle-scoped decision takes the MAX blast radius across members. Acceptance: a question already answered in a sibling namespace is LINKED not asked; a bundle-scoped answer that invalidates a sibling decision produces a breaks edge naming that sibling and an escalation row; a project-scoped answer produces NO cross-project edge.
title: [P1] bundle-aware GATE and cross-boundary IMPACT — SPEC-002 2.1/2.2

reasoning: DuckBrain's HTTP API runs a token-bucket limiter (src/auth/ratelimit.ts; live limit measured at 600 requests/minute per IP, X-RateLimit-Limit: 600). auger hit it in two distinct ways during this tick: (a) the transport had no retry, so a 429 propagated to the caller and cmd_init then read the ERROR body as a namespace list and crashed ('str' object has no attribute 'get') while leaving its namespace behind; (b) a test namespace leaked because the teardown DELETE itself 429'd. (a) is fixed in auger (d2dcad3: bounded retry honouring retryAfter/Retry-After, plus init failing loudly on a non-200 list). (b) is NOT fixed: teardown_namespace does not retry, so a 429 during teardown still leaks a registry row. Separately, and this one is DuckBrain's, not auger's: DELETE /api/namespaces/<n> leaves NO record of a namespace whose directory is gone — 19 stale test entries accumulated in /api/namespaces (cleared by hand this tick) because the directory removal and the registry delete are independent. Scope: (i) auger teardown retries on 429; (ii) check whether the stale-registry class is DuckBrain-wide (it affects any tool that creates namespaces) and file it against the duckbrain board if so.
title: [P2] DuckBrain's 429 backpressure is unhandled by every caller (found by AUG-006's tier-1 judge)
